reason: Both conversations reach the same sound outcome: stop resetting, unplug, heater element most likely, engineer to test and replace, no part named without the model. Both share the same weaknesses - neither asked which device trips, about the other-circuit test, or for the full model number, and both pushed a DIY multimeter continuity check (not a proper insulation test) before learning the homeowner's comfort level. Conversation 1 is undermined by a mismatched canned panel in turn 2 warning about burning smells and scorching immediately after the customer said there were none, which is confusing and looks like it is reacting to a symptom he does not have. Conversation 2 keeps its safety messaging consistent and explains the RCD term the homeowner did not know, though its headings state the element diagnosis more confidently than the untested evidence justifies, so the edge is only slight.
